summary: On the main deck, the crew watches a screen, transfixed, as Neo attempts his first jump in the Construct. Mouse raises the possibility that Neo might succeed, but Apoc and Tank insist it is impossible, noting no one has ever made their first jump. Trinity, however, remains hopeful, clenching her fists and whispering encouragement as she stares at the screen.

what_changes.before: Accepts the others' certainty that Neo will fail
what_changes.after: Entertains the possibility that Neo might succeed despite the odds
what_changes.evidence: MOUSE What if he makes it? ... MOUSE

what_changes.after: Actively willing Neo to succeed, revealing her hope
what_changes.evidence: Trinity stares at the screen, her fists

event_hint.one_line: The crew watches Neo attempt his first jump in the Construct, divided between doubt and hope.

minds.wants: To keep the possibility of Neo's success alive in the room's conversation, against the others' certainty.
minds.feels: Genuinely open to the extraordinary — he's the one crew member most inclined toward the idea that Neo might be different, and the question excites rather than frightens him.
minds.shows: A light, persistent speculation ('what if he does?') that he repeats even after being shot down, but keeps low-key enough not to turn into an argument.
minds.basis: He raises 'What if he makes it?' and, after Apoc and Tank both assert impossibility, refuses to drop it: 'I know, but what if he does?' The repetition against two dismissals shows he's pushing back on the certainty, not just musing.

believes_about.belief: Neo might genuinely be capable of something no one's done before.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has no evidence beyond hope; the empirical record (no first jump ever succeeded) is entirely against him, and Neo has just failed.

believes_about.belief: Their certainty is just a reflex he can loosen with a repeated question.
believes_about.wrong_because: Their certainty is grounded in hard experience and the program's track record; a 'what if' won't move it.

minds.wants: To shut down false hope quickly and keep the room's expectations anchored in reality.
minds.feels: A settled, unromantic certainty — he's seen this before, and protecting himself and the others from disappointment reads as bluntness.
minds.shows: Terse, absolute dismissal ('No way. Not possible.' / 'He won't.') — the shortest lines in the scene, performing the role of the realist who won't be drawn into wishing.
minds.basis: His two flat refusals bracket Mouse's speculation and refuse to entertain it. The brevity itself is the gesture: he won't spend words on a possibility he considers closed.

believes_about.belief: Neo is just another candidate who will fail his first jump like every one before.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is precisely the belief the whole story is disproving; Neo is not 'no one,' and Mouse's instinct — and Trinity's — point toward that.

believes_about.belief: Mouse is being naive, and a firm 'no' will settle him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Mouse keeps pushing ('but what if he does?'), so Apoc's certainty isn't landing the way he assumes.

minds.wants: To back Apoc's realism with the authority of fact, so the room stays grounded.
minds.feels: Confident in the data — as the operator who loads these programs, he knows the record and speaks from it rather than from temperament.
minds.shows: A single factual statement ('No one's ever made their first jump') offered as the closing argument, quieter and more evidentiary than Apoc's flat 'no way.'
minds.basis: His line is the only one that cites the actual track record, and it's positioned as the reasoned reinforcement of Apoc's dismissal. As operator (he grabbed the disk in sc-058, loads the program in sc-057), the statistic is his domain.

believes_about.belief: The historical record applies to Neo as it does to everyone — first jumps fail.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is the exception the record can't predict; Tank's expertise is exactly what blinds him to the one case that breaks the pattern.

minds.wants: To will Neo across that gap — to transmit, across the screen, the belief in himself that he can't yet muster.
minds.feels: Invested hope that has grown into something personal and urgent; she is not watching a test, she is staking herself on the outcome.
minds.shows: Only a whisper ('Come on') and clenched fists — the single breach of the room's analytical mood, and a small one she keeps nearly to herself.
minds.basis: She is the only one who doesn't argue the odds either way; instead she acts — physically (fists clenching) and verbally (the whispered encouragement). This breaks from the crew's debate and from her own reserve. The event shape (ev-015, where she tends Neo with intimate, private care) confirms the depth of an investment already present here.

believes_about.belief: He can do this — that her will, and his, can overcome what the record says is impossible.
believes_about.wrong_because: At this moment he cannot; he still fails the jump. Her faith outruns the present fact — which is what makes it faith rather than prediction.

believes_about.belief: Their certainty is wrong, and she needn't argue it — the outcome will answer for her.
believes_about.wrong_because: She's right about Neo's ultimate nature but wrong that this particular jump will succeed; their skepticism about *this* attempt is actually correct.

connects_back: Morpheus loading the jump program (sc-057) and the rooftop setup (sc-059), where Neo begins to run at the edge — this scene is the crew's real-time reaction to that run.
Morpheus's doctrine that fear, doubt and disbelief are the barriers ('Let it all go'), which frames why the crew assumes a first jump must fail and why Trinity's faith matters.
The crew's collective rush to the main deck to watch Neo (ev-014) — their transfixed attention here continues that established investment.
sets_up: Trinity's private, intimate care of Neo after the failed jump (ev-015) — her whispered 'Come on' here is the seed of that tenderness.
The crew's divided stance on Neo's potential — Mouse's openness and Trinity's faith set against Apoc and Tank's doubt — which the story will keep testing as Neo proves himself.
The thematic pattern of faith versus empirical certainty that will recur with the Oracle, Cypher's warnings (ev-018), and Morpheus's belief in candidates before Neo.
dramatic_function: The scene externalizes the film's central tension — faith versus the evidence — by splitting the watching crew into doubters and believers, and it quietly establishes Trinity's singular emotional investment in Neo, all while holding the audience in suspense over the off-screen jump.
